CHAPTER 14 - SIMILARITY OF TRIANGLES

Introduction

In everyday life we constantly meet objects that have the same shape but different sizes: a photograph and its enlargement, a model aeroplane and the real one, two maps of India drawn to different scales, or the image of a tree and its shadow. Such figures are said to be SIMILAR. Similarity is one of the most useful ideas in geometry because it lets us calculate lengths and distances that we cannot measure directly - the height of a tall tree, the width of a river, or the distance of a ship from the shore. In this chapter we study similarity carefully, mainly for triangles, and develop the tests (criteria) that decide when two triangles are similar. We then use these tests to prove the Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales' theorem), the theorem on the ratio of areas of similar triangles, and finally the celebrated Pythagoras theorem, which turns out to be a beautiful application of similar triangles.

14.1 SIMILAR FIGURES

Two figures are said to be SIMILAR if they have exactly the SAME SHAPE, though not necessarily the same size. All squares are similar to one another; all circles are similar; all equilateral triangles are similar. However, a square and a rectangle are NOT similar, because although both have four right angles their shapes differ. Two figures that are similar AND equal in size are CONGRUENT - congruence is a special case of similarity in which the ratio of corresponding sides is 1. So every pair of congruent figures is similar, but similar figures need not be congruent.

When two polygons are similar, two conditions hold together:
 (i) their corresponding angles are equal, and
 (ii) their corresponding sides are in the same ratio (proportional).
The common value of the ratio of corresponding sides is called the SCALE FACTOR (or ratio of similitude). If a map is drawn to a scale of 1 : 50000, the scale factor between map and ground is 1/50000.

14.2 SIMILAR TRIANGLES

Triangles are the simplest polygons, and for triangles the two conditions above are closely linked. Two triangles ABC and DEF are SIMILAR (written triangle ABC ~ triangle DEF) if:
 (i) angle A = angle D, angle B = angle E, angle C = angle F, and
 (ii) AB/DE = BC/EF = CA/FD.
The symbol ~ is read 'is similar to'. The ORDER of the letters matters: writing ABC ~ DEF means A corresponds to D, B to E, and C to F. Corresponding sides are the sides opposite to equal angles. It is a remarkable fact that for triangles you do not have to check BOTH conditions - checking a suitable part of one condition forces the other. This gives the similarity criteria below.

14.3 CRITERIA FOR SIMILARITY OF TRIANGLES

(a) AAA (or AA) similarity criterion. If in two triangles the corresponding angles are equal, then their corresponding sides are proportional and hence the triangles are similar. Because the three angles of a triangle always add to 180°, if two pairs of angles are equal the third pair is automatically equal; so it is enough to show that TWO angles of one triangle equal two angles of the other. This shorter version is called the AA (angle-angle) criterion. Example: if angle A = angle D = 50° and angle B = angle E = 60°, then triangle ABC ~ triangle DEF at once.

(b) SSS similarity criterion. If in two triangles the corresponding sides are in the same ratio (proportional), then their corresponding angles are equal and the triangles are similar. For example, if AB/DE = BC/EF = CA/FD = 2/3, then triangle ABC ~ triangle DEF. Note the difference from SSS congruence: here the sides need not be equal, only proportional.

(c) SAS similarity criterion. If one angle of a triangle equals one angle of the other triangle AND the sides including these equal angles are proportional, then the triangles are similar. That is, if angle A = angle D and AB/DE = AC/DF, then triangle ABC ~ triangle DEF. The equal angle must be the INCLUDED angle (the angle between the two proportional sides).

These three criteria - AAA/AA, SSS, SAS - are the basic tools. Once similarity is established, ALL pairs of corresponding sides are in the same ratio, which lets us find unknown lengths.

Worked example. In triangle ABC, angle B = 90°. A point in the configuration gives two triangles with angle A = 35° each and a shared right angle, so by AA they are similar; corresponding sides are then proportional and any missing length can be found by cross-multiplication.

14.4 BASIC PROPORTIONALITY THEOREM (THALES' THEOREM)

Statement. If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides at distinct points, then it divides those two sides in the same ratio.

In triangle ABC, let a line DE be drawn parallel to BC, meeting AB at D and AC at E. Then
   AD/DB = AE/EC.

Proof (using areas). Join BE and CD. Triangles ADE and BDE have the same height (the perpendicular distance from E to line AB), so the ratio of their areas equals the ratio of their bases: area(ADE)/area(BDE) = AD/DB. Similarly, taking the height from D to line AC, area(ADE)/area(CDE) = AE/EC. Now triangles BDE and CDE stand on the same base DE and lie between the same parallels DE and BC, so they have EQUAL areas: area(BDE) = area(CDE). Therefore the two left-hand ratios are equal, giving AD/DB = AE/EC. This proves the Basic Proportionality Theorem (BPT).

Converse of BPT. If a line divides any two sides of a triangle in the same ratio, then the line is parallel to the third side. That is, in triangle ABC, if D lies on AB and E on AC with AD/DB = AE/EC, then DE is parallel to BC. The converse is used to PROVE that lines are parallel.

A very useful consequence: if DE || BC in triangle ABC, then triangle ADE ~ triangle ABC (by AA, since angle A is common and angle ADE = angle ABC as corresponding angles), and therefore AD/AB = AE/AC = DE/BC.

14.5 AREAS OF SIMILAR TRIANGLES

Theorem. The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the ratio of the SQUARES of their corresponding sides.

If triangle ABC ~ triangle DEF, then
   area(ABC)/area(DEF) = (AB/DE)^2 = (BC/EF)^2 = (CA/FD)^2.

Sketch of proof. Draw altitudes AM and DN to the bases BC and EF. Area(ABC) = (1/2) x BC x AM and area(DEF) = (1/2) x EF x DN, so area(ABC)/area(DEF) = (BC x AM)/(EF x DN). Because the triangles are similar, BC/EF = AB/DE, and the right triangles ABM and DEN are similar (angle B = angle E, right angles at M and N), giving AM/DN = AB/DE = BC/EF. Substituting, area(ABC)/area(DEF) = (BC/EF) x (BC/EF) = (BC/EF)^2. So areas grow as the SQUARE of the scale factor. If two similar triangles have sides in ratio 2 : 3, their areas are in ratio 4 : 9. The same law explains why doubling the side of a photograph quadruples the paper area.

14.6 PYTHAGORAS THEOREM AND ITS CONVERSE

Theorem (Pythagoras). In a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides. If triangle ABC is right-angled at B, then AC^2 = AB^2 + BC^2, where AC is the hypotenuse.

Proof using similar triangles. Let triangle ABC be right-angled at B. Draw BD perpendicular to the hypotenuse AC, with D on AC. This altitude creates two smaller triangles, ADB and BDC, each similar to the whole triangle ABC (each shares an angle with ABC and has a right angle). From triangle ADB ~ triangle ABC we get AB/AC = AD/AB, so AB^2 = AC x AD. From triangle BDC ~ triangle ABC we get BC/AC = DC/BC, so BC^2 = AC x DC. Adding, AB^2 + BC^2 = AC x (AD + DC) = AC x AC = AC^2. Hence AC^2 = AB^2 + BC^2.

Converse of Pythagoras theorem. In a triangle, if the square of one side equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides, then the angle opposite the first side is a right angle. For example, a triangle with sides 3, 4, 5 satisfies 3^2 + 4^2 = 9 + 16 = 25 = 5^2, so it is right-angled (the right angle being opposite the side of length 5). Triples such as (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17) and (7, 24, 25) are called Pythagorean triples.

14.7 APPLICATIONS - HEIGHTS, DISTANCES AND SHADOWS

Similar triangles let us find lengths we cannot reach. A common method uses SHADOWS. At a given moment the sun's rays fall at the same angle everywhere, so a vertical pole and a vertical tower cast shadows that form similar triangles (each has a right angle at the ground and a common angle of elevation of the sun). Therefore
   (height of pole)/(length of pole's shadow) = (height of tower)/(length of tower's shadow).
Example: a 6 m pole casts a 4 m shadow while a tower casts a 20 m shadow at the same time. Then height of tower = 6 x (20/4) = 30 m.

The same idea finds the width of a river or the distance of an inaccessible object by setting up two similar triangles on the ground and measuring the accessible sides. Pythagoras theorem is used whenever right angles are involved - for the length of a ladder leaning on a wall, the diagonal of a rectangular field, or the straight-line distance between two points reached by moving east then north.

SUMMARY

- Two figures are SIMILAR if they have the same shape; corresponding angles are equal and corresponding sides are proportional. Congruent figures are the special case with scale factor 1.
- Two triangles are similar (~) when their angles are equal and their sides are proportional. For triangles, three criteria suffice: AAA/AA (angles equal), SSS (sides proportional) and SAS (one equal angle between proportional sides).
- Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales): a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides in the same ratio (AD/DB = AE/EC). Its converse proves parallelism.
- The ratio of areas of two similar triangles equals the ratio of the squares of corresponding sides: area ratio = (side ratio)^2.
- Pythagoras theorem: in a right triangle, hypotenuse^2 = sum of squares of the other two sides; it follows from similar triangles formed by the altitude to the hypotenuse. Its converse tests whether a triangle is right-angled.
- Similar triangles and Pythagoras theorem are used to find heights, distances, shadows and diagonals that cannot be measured directly.

topics.name: Similar Figures and Triangles
topics.description: Meaning of similarity; similar figures have the same shape; corresponding angles equal and corresponding sides proportional; congruence as a special case; the ~ notation and correspondence of vertices for triangles.

topics.name: AA/AAA Similarity
topics.description: The angle-angle-angle (and its short form angle-angle) criterion: if corresponding angles of two triangles are equal, the triangles are similar and their sides are proportional.

topics.name: SSS and SAS Similarity
topics.description: The SSS criterion (all corresponding sides proportional) and the SAS criterion (one equal angle included between two proportional sides) for establishing similarity of triangles.

topics.name: Basic Proportionality Theorem
topics.description: Thales' theorem: a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides in the same ratio; its area-based proof; and the converse used to prove lines parallel.

topics.name: Areas of Similar Triangles
topics.description: The theorem that the ratio of the areas of two similar triangles equals the ratio of the squares of their corresponding sides, and its use in numerical problems.

topics.name: Pythagoras Theorem and Applications
topics.description: Pythagoras theorem and its converse derived from similar triangles, Pythagorean triples, and applications to heights, distances, shadows, ladders and diagonals.

learning_outcomes.description: Explain what similar figures and similar triangles are, and state the two conditions (equal angles, proportional sides) that define similarity.
State and apply the AAA / AA similarity criterion to show two triangles are similar from their angles.
Use the SSS and SAS similarity criteria to test whether two triangles are similar and to find unknown sides.
State and prove the Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales' theorem) and explain its converse.
Apply the Basic Proportionality Theorem and its converse to compute unknown segment lengths and to prove lines parallel.
Use the theorem that areas of similar triangles are in the ratio of the squares of corresponding sides to solve numerical problems.
State and prove the Pythagoras theorem using similar triangles, and use its converse to identify right-angled triangles.
Apply similar triangles and the Pythagoras theorem to find heights, distances, shadow lengths and diagonals in real situations.

chapter_summary.title: Similarity of Triangles - Chapter Summary
chapter_summary.intro: This chapter explains when two figures have the same shape (are similar), gives the AA, SSS and SAS tests for similar triangles, proves the Basic Proportionality Theorem and the area-ratio theorem, and derives Pythagoras theorem from similar triangles - then uses all of these to find heights, distances and shadows.

sections.heading: Similar figures and triangles
bullets: Similar figures have exactly the same SHAPE but may differ in size; all circles, all squares and all equilateral triangles are similar.
Two conditions define similarity of polygons: corresponding angles are equal AND corresponding sides are in the same ratio (the scale factor).
Congruent figures are a special case of similar figures with scale factor 1; every pair of congruent figures is similar but not conversely.
For triangles we write triangle ABC ~ triangle DEF; the order of the letters fixes which vertices, angles and sides correspond.

sections.heading: Criteria for similarity
bullets: AAA / AA: if corresponding angles are equal the triangles are similar; because angles sum to 180 degrees, checking two pairs is enough.
SSS: if all three pairs of corresponding sides are proportional, the triangles are similar.
SAS: if one pair of angles is equal and the two sides INCLUDING those angles are proportional, the triangles are similar.
Once similarity is proved, every pair of corresponding sides shares the same ratio, so unknown sides follow by cross-multiplication.

sections.heading: Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales)
bullets: A line drawn parallel to one side of a triangle cutting the other two sides divides them in the same ratio: AD/DB = AE/EC.
The theorem is proved using areas of triangles that share a base and lie between the same parallels (equal areas).
The converse states: if a line divides two sides of a triangle in the same ratio, it is parallel to the third side.
If DE || BC then triangle ADE ~ triangle ABC, so AD/AB = AE/AC = DE/BC.

sections.heading: Areas of similar triangles
bullets: The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles equals the ratio of the SQUARES of their corresponding sides.
In symbols, if triangle ABC ~ triangle DEF then area(ABC)/area(DEF) = (AB/DE)^2.
Sides in ratio 2:3 give areas in ratio 4:9; the area always changes as the square of the scale factor.

sections.heading: Pythagoras theorem and applications
bullets: In a right triangle the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides: AC^2 = AB^2 + BC^2.
The proof drops the altitude from the right angle to the hypotenuse, creating two triangles each similar to the original.
The converse identifies right triangles: if one side squared equals the sum of the other two squared, the opposite angle is 90 degrees.
Similar triangles and Pythagoras theorem find tree heights, river widths, shadow lengths, ladder lengths and diagonals.

key_takeaways: Similar figures have the same shape: equal corresponding angles and proportional corresponding sides; congruence is the scale-factor-1 case.
Three tests establish similar triangles - AA (angles), SSS (proportional sides) and SAS (equal included angle with proportional sides).
Basic Proportionality Theorem: a line parallel to one side divides the other two sides in the same ratio; its converse proves parallelism.
The ratio of areas of two similar triangles equals the ratio of the squares of corresponding sides.
Pythagoras theorem (hypotenuse squared = sum of squares of the legs) is a direct consequence of similar triangles.
The converse of Pythagoras theorem tests whether a triangle is right-angled; 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17 are common triples.
Similar triangles and Pythagoras theorem let us compute heights, distances and shadows that cannot be measured directly.

glossary.definition: Figures having the same shape but not necessarily the same size; corresponding angles are equal and corresponding sides are proportional.
Figures identical in both shape and size; a special case of similar figures with scale factor 1.
The common ratio of the lengths of corresponding sides of two similar figures; also called the ratio of similitude.
Two triangles whose corresponding angles are equal and whose corresponding sides are proportional; written with the symbol ~.
If corresponding angles of two triangles are equal the triangles are similar; two equal angle pairs suffice since angles sum to 180 degrees.
If the three pairs of corresponding sides of two triangles are in the same ratio, the triangles are similar.
If one pair of angles is equal and the sides including these angles are proportional, the triangles are similar.
Thales' theorem: a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides in the same ratio, AD/DB = AE/EC.
If a line divides two sides of a triangle in the same ratio, then the line is parallel to the third side.
In similar triangles, the sides that lie opposite to equal angles; they occur in the same ratio.
The ratio of areas of two similar triangles equals the ratio of the squares of their corresponding sides.
In a right-angled triangle the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides.
If in a triangle the square of one side equals the sum of the squares of the other two, the angle opposite that side is 90 degrees.
Three whole numbers a, b, c with a^2 + b^2 = c^2, such as (3,4,5), (5,12,13) and (8,15,17).
The side opposite the right angle in a right-angled triangle; it is the longest side.

worksheet.title: Worksheet - Similarity of Triangles
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Draw rough figures where helpful, show full working for proofs and numericals, and give answers with correct units.

questions.question: State and prove the Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales' theorem). In triangle ABC a line DE is drawn parallel to BC meeting AB at D and AC at E; show that AD/DB = AE/EC.
questions.answer:
Statement: If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides in distinct points, then it divides the two sides in the same ratio.
Given: triangle ABC with DE || BC, D on AB, E on AC. To prove: AD/DB = AE/EC.
Construction: Join BE and CD; draw EM perpendicular to AB and DN perpendicular to AC.
Proof: area(ADE) = (1/2) x AD x EM and area(BDE) = (1/2) x DB x EM, so area(ADE)/area(BDE) = AD/DB. Likewise area(ADE)/area(CDE) = AE/EC. Triangles BDE and CDE have the same base DE and lie between the same parallels DE and BC, so area(BDE) = area(CDE). Hence area(ADE)/area(BDE) = area(ADE)/area(CDE), which gives AD/DB = AE/EC. Proved.

questions.question: In triangle ABC, DE || BC with D on AB and E on AC. If AD = 3 cm, DB = 5 cm and AE = 4.5 cm, find EC.
questions.answer: By the Basic Proportionality Theorem, AD/DB = AE/EC. So 3/5 = 4.5/EC, giving EC = (4.5 x 5)/3 = 22.5/3 = 7.5 cm.

questions.question: Two triangles have sides 4, 6, 8 cm and 6, 9, 12 cm. Are they similar? Justify by the correct criterion.
questions.answer: Compare corresponding sides in increasing order: 4/6 = 2/3, 6/9 = 2/3, 8/12 = 2/3. All three ratios are equal (2/3), so by the SSS similarity criterion the triangles are similar. The scale factor is 2/3.
questions.explanation: SSS similarity: all three side ratios equal.

questions.question: In triangle ABC, angle A = angle of triangle PQR at P, and AB/PQ = AC/PR = 2/5. Name the similarity criterion used and find BC if QR = 15 cm.
questions.answer: One angle (angle A = angle P) is equal and the two sides including that angle are proportional (AB/PQ = AC/PR = 2/5), so by the SAS similarity criterion triangle ABC ~ triangle PQR. Then BC/QR = 2/5, so BC = (2/5) x 15 = 6 cm.
questions.explanation: SAS similarity, then use the common ratio.

questions.question: Triangle ABC ~ triangle DEF. If AB = 5 cm, DE = 8 cm and the area of triangle ABC is 25 cm^2, find the area of triangle DEF.
questions.answer: By the theorem on areas of similar triangles, area(ABC)/area(DEF) = (AB/DE)^2 = (5/8)^2 = 25/64. So 25/area(DEF) = 25/64, giving area(DEF) = 64 cm^2. (Check: the side ratio is 5:8, the area ratio is 25:64, and 25 x 64/25 = 64.)
questions.explanation: Area ratio equals square of side ratio.

questions.question: A ladder 13 m long rests against a vertical wall with its foot 5 m from the wall. How high up the wall does the ladder reach?
questions.answer: The wall, ground and ladder form a right triangle with the right angle at the foot of the wall. Let the height be h. By Pythagoras theorem, 13^2 = h^2 + 5^2, so 169 = h^2 + 25, h^2 = 144, h = 12 m. The ladder reaches 12 m up the wall.

questions.question: A triangle has sides 9 cm, 12 cm and 15 cm. Show that it is right-angled and name the right angle.
questions.answer: Check the converse of Pythagoras theorem. The longest side is 15 cm. 9^2 + 12^2 = 81 + 144 = 225 and 15^2 = 225. Since 9^2 + 12^2 = 15^2, the triangle is right-angled, and the right angle is the one opposite the longest side (15 cm).

questions.question: Prove the Pythagoras theorem using similar triangles: in triangle ABC right-angled at B, show that AC^2 = AB^2 + BC^2.
questions.answer:
Given: triangle ABC with angle B = 90 degrees. Construction: draw BD perpendicular to AC, D on AC.
In triangles ADB and ABC: angle A is common and both have a right angle (angle ADB = angle ABC = 90 degrees), so by AA, triangle ADB ~ triangle ABC. Hence AD/AB = AB/AC, giving AB^2 = AD x AC. (1)
In triangles BDC and ABC: angle C is common and both have a right angle, so triangle BDC ~ triangle ABC. Hence DC/BC = BC/AC, giving BC^2 = DC x AC. (2)
Adding (1) and (2): AB^2 + BC^2 = AD x AC + DC x AC = (AD + DC) x AC = AC x AC = AC^2. Therefore AC^2 = AB^2 + BC^2. Proved.
questions.explanation: Altitude to hypotenuse creates two similar triangles.

questions.question: A vertical pole 6 m high casts a shadow 4 m long on the ground. At the same time a tower casts a shadow 28 m long. Find the height of the tower.
questions.answer: At the same time of day the sun's rays make equal angles, so the pole and its shadow form a triangle similar to the tower and its shadow (each has a right angle at the ground and equal angle of elevation). Therefore (height of pole)/(shadow of pole) = (height of tower)/(shadow of tower): 6/4 = H/28, so H = (6 x 28)/4 = 168/4 = 42 m. The tower is 42 m high.
questions.explanation: Similar triangles from equal sun angle.

questions.question: In triangle ABC, DE || BC. If AD/DB = 2/3, find the ratio AD : AB.
questions.answer: Since AD/DB = 2/3, take AD = 2k and DB = 3k. Then AB = AD + DB = 5k, so AD : AB = 2k : 5k = 2 : 5.
questions.explanation: Convert AD/DB to AD/AB by adding parts.

questions.question: Figures with the same shape but not necessarily the same size are called ____.
The scale factor of two congruent figures is ____.
If corresponding ____ of two triangles are equal, the triangles are similar (AAA).
Two triangles are similar by AA; if their sides are in ratio 1:3 and one side is 4 cm, the corresponding side is ____ cm.
In SSS similarity all three pairs of corresponding sides are ____.
Triangles with sides 3,4,5 and 9,12,15 are similar with scale factor ____.
questions.explanation: Each side of the larger is 3 times the smaller.

questions.question: In triangle ABC, if DE || BC then AD/DB = AE/____.
If DE || BC in triangle ABC, then triangle ADE is ____ to triangle ABC.
In triangle ABC, DE || BC. If AD=3, DB=6 and AE=4, then EC = ____.
The theorem used to prove that a line is parallel to a side of a triangle is the ____ of the Basic Proportionality Theorem.
The ratio of areas of two similar triangles equals the ratio of the ____ of corresponding sides.
Two similar triangles have sides in ratio 5:2. The ratio of their areas is ____.
In a right triangle, hypotenuse^2 = ____ + (base)^2 (perpendicular squared plus base squared).
A right triangle has legs 9 and 12; its hypotenuse is ____.
A 5 m pole casts a 3 m shadow; a tree casts a 12 m shadow at the same time. The tree is ____ m tall.
Define similar figures and give one example of figures that are always similar.
questions.answer: Two figures are similar if they have the same shape but not necessarily the same size; their corresponding angles are equal and corresponding sides are proportional. Example: any two squares (or any two circles) are always similar.

questions.question: How is congruence related to similarity?
questions.answer: Congruent figures have the same shape AND the same size, so their corresponding sides are equal (ratio 1) and corresponding angles are equal. Congruence is therefore a special case of similarity with scale factor 1. Every pair of congruent figures is similar, but similar figures need not be congruent.

questions.question: The sides of a triangle are 3 cm, 4 cm, 6 cm. A similar triangle has its shortest side 9 cm. Find its other two sides.
questions.answer: The scale factor is 9/3 = 3. So the other sides are 4 x 3 = 12 cm and 6 x 3 = 18 cm. The similar triangle has sides 9 cm, 12 cm, 18 cm.
questions.explanation: Multiply each side by the scale factor 3.

questions.question: State the AAA (and AA) similarity criterion.
questions.answer: AAA: if the corresponding angles of two triangles are equal, then their corresponding sides are proportional and the triangles are similar. Since the angle sum of a triangle is 180 degrees, showing two pairs of angles equal forces the third pair equal; hence the short form AA (angle-angle) is sufficient.
questions.explanation: AAA criterion, with AA short form.

questions.question: In triangle ABC, DE is drawn with angle ADE = angle ACB. Show triangle ADE ~ triangle ACB and hence, if AD=3, AC=6, AE=4, find AB.
questions.answer: In triangles ADE and ACB, angle A is common and angle ADE = angle ACB (given). By AA, triangle ADE ~ triangle ACB. Hence corresponding sides are proportional: AD/AC = AE/AB. So 3/6 = 4/AB, giving AB = (4 x 6)/3 = 8. AB = 8 units.

questions.question: In triangle ABC right-angled at B, BD is drawn perpendicular to AC. Name a triangle similar to triangle ABC and give the reason.
questions.answer: Triangle ADB ~ triangle ABC (also triangle BDC ~ triangle ABC). Reason: in triangle ADB and triangle ABC, angle A is common and both have a right angle (angle ADB = angle ABC = 90 degrees), so by the AA criterion they are similar.
questions.explanation: Altitude to hypotenuse gives AA similar triangles.

questions.question: State the SSS and SAS similarity criteria.
questions.answer: SSS: if the three pairs of corresponding sides of two triangles are proportional, the triangles are similar. SAS: if one angle of a triangle equals one angle of the other and the sides including these angles are proportional, the triangles are similar.

questions.question: Two triangles have sides 4 cm, 5 cm, 6 cm and 8 cm, 10 cm, 12 cm. Are they similar? Justify and give the scale factor.
questions.answer: Arrange corresponding sides and compare ratios: 4/8 = 1/2, 5/10 = 1/2, 6/12 = 1/2. All three ratios are equal, so by the SSS similarity criterion the triangles are similar. The scale factor (smaller to larger) is 1:2.

questions.question: In triangles ABC and DEF, angle A = angle D, AB = 4, AC = 6, DE = 6, DF = 9. Show that they are similar.
questions.answer: The angle A = angle D is equal and the including sides satisfy AB/DE = 4/6 = 2/3 and AC/DF = 6/9 = 2/3. Since the two sides including the equal angle are proportional, by the SAS similarity criterion triangle ABC ~ triangle DEF.

questions.question: State the Basic Proportionality Theorem and write the 'Given, To prove and Construction' you would use to prove it.
questions.answer: Statement: If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to meet the other two sides in distinct points, it divides those sides in the same ratio. Given: triangle ABC with DE || BC, D on AB, E on AC. To prove: AD/DB = AE/EC. Construction: join BE and CD, and draw EM perpendicular to AB and DN perpendicular to AC (for the area proof).

questions.question: Why are triangles BDE and CDE equal in area in the proof of BPT?
questions.answer: Triangles BDE and CDE stand on the same base DE and lie between the same pair of parallel lines DE and BC. Triangles on the same base and between the same parallels have equal areas, so area(BDE) = area(CDE). This equality is the key step that gives AD/DB = AE/EC.
questions.explanation: Same base, same parallels -> equal area.

questions.question: In triangle ABC, DE || BC. If AD = 4 cm, AB = 9 cm and AE = 6 cm, find AC.
questions.answer: Since DE || BC, AD/AB = AE/AC. So 4/9 = 6/AC, giving AC = (6 x 9)/4 = 54/4 = 13.5 cm.

questions.question: In triangle ABC, points D on AB and E on AC satisfy AD = 2 cm, DB = 3 cm, AE = 2.8 cm, EC = 4.2 cm. Determine whether DE is parallel to BC.
questions.answer: Compute the ratios: AD/DB = 2/3 and AE/EC = 2.8/4.2 = 28/42 = 2/3. Since AD/DB = AE/EC, by the converse of the Basic Proportionality Theorem the line DE is parallel to BC.
questions.explanation: Converse of BPT: equal ratios -> parallel.

questions.question: In triangle ABC, DE || BC. If AD/DB = 2/3 and AC = 10 cm, find AE.
questions.answer: When DE || BC, AD/DB = AE/EC = 2/3. Let AE = 2k, EC = 3k, so AC = 5k = 10, giving k = 2. Therefore AE = 2k = 4 cm.

questions.question: In triangle ABC, D on AB and E on AC with DE || BC. If AD = 3 cm, DB = x, AE = 4 cm and EC = x + 3, find x.
questions.answer: By the Basic Proportionality Theorem, AD/DB = AE/EC, so 3/x = 4/(x + 3). Cross-multiplying gives 3(x + 3) = 4x, i.e. 3x + 9 = 4x, so x = 9 cm. Check: AD/DB = 3/9 = 1/3 and AE/EC = 4/12 = 1/3, which are equal, confirming DB = 9 cm.
questions.explanation: Set up AD/DB = AE/EC and solve the linear equation.

questions.question: State the theorem on areas of similar triangles.
questions.answer: The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the ratio of the squares of their corresponding sides. If triangle ABC ~ triangle DEF then area(ABC)/area(DEF) = (AB/DE)^2 = (BC/EF)^2 = (CA/FD)^2.
questions.explanation: Area ratio = square of side ratio.

questions.question: Triangle ABC ~ triangle PQR. If AB = 4 cm, PQ = 6 cm and area of triangle PQR is 45 cm^2, find the area of triangle ABC.
The areas of two similar triangles are 81 cm^2 and 49 cm^2. Find the ratio of their corresponding sides.
questions.answer: Ratio of areas = 81:49. Ratio of corresponding sides = sqrt(81):sqrt(49) = 9:7.
questions.explanation: Take the square root of the area ratio.

questions.question: Two similar triangles have corresponding medians in the ratio 3:5. Find the ratio of their areas.
questions.answer: Corresponding medians scale like the sides (linear ratio), so the side ratio is 3:5. The ratio of areas is (3:5)^2 = 9:25.

questions.question: State the Pythagoras theorem and outline how it is proved using similar triangles.
questions.answer: Pythagoras theorem: in a right triangle the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides (AC^2 = AB^2 + BC^2 for right angle at B). Proof outline: drop the altitude BD from the right angle B to the hypotenuse AC. Then triangle ADB ~ triangle ABC and triangle BDC ~ triangle ABC (AA). These give AB^2 = AC x AD and BC^2 = AC x DC. Adding, AB^2 + BC^2 = AC(AD + DC) = AC x AC = AC^2.
questions.explanation: Altitude to hypotenuse creates two similar triangles.

questions.question: Using the converse of Pythagoras theorem, check whether a triangle with sides 10 cm, 24 cm and 26 cm is right-angled.
questions.answer: Longest side 26. Check 10^2 + 24^2 = 100 + 576 = 676 and 26^2 = 676. Since 10^2 + 24^2 = 26^2, by the converse of Pythagoras theorem the triangle is right-angled, with the right angle opposite the 26 cm side.

questions.question: Write any two Pythagorean triples and verify one of them.
questions.answer: Two triples: (3, 4, 5) and (5, 12, 13). Verification of (5, 12, 13): 5^2 + 12^2 = 25 + 144 = 169 = 13^2, which satisfies a^2 + b^2 = c^2.

questions.question: In triangle ABC right-angled at B, BD is perpendicular to AC. If AD = 4 cm and DC = 9 cm, find BD and hence AB.
questions.answer: BD is the geometric mean of AD and DC: BD^2 = AD x DC = 4 x 9 = 36, so BD = 6 cm. Also AB^2 = AC x AD = (4+9) x 4 = 13 x 4 = 52, so AB = sqrt(52) = 2 sqrt(13) cm (approximately 7.21 cm).

questions.question: A ladder 17 m long reaches a window 15 m above the ground on one side of a street. Find the distance of the foot of the ladder from the wall.
questions.answer: The wall, ground and ladder form a right triangle with the ladder as hypotenuse. Let the base be b. Then 17^2 = 15^2 + b^2, so 289 = 225 + b^2, b^2 = 64, b = 8 m. The foot of the ladder is 8 m from the wall.

questions.question: A vertical tower casts a shadow 40 m long, while a vertical pole 6 m high casts a shadow 8 m long at the same time. Find the height of the tower and name the property used.
questions.answer: At the same time of day the sun's rays make equal angles, so the pole and the tower with their shadows form similar right triangles (AA similarity). Therefore height/shadow is the same: 6/8 = H/40, giving H = (6 x 40)/8 = 30 m. The tower is 30 m high. Property used: similarity of triangles (equal angle of elevation of the sun).
questions.explanation: Similar triangles from equal sun angle.

questions.question: A man goes 15 m due west and then 8 m due north. How far is he from the starting point?
questions.answer: The path forms a right angle at the turning point. Distance = sqrt(15^2 + 8^2) = sqrt(225 + 64) = sqrt(289) = 17 m. He is 17 m from the start.

questions.question: Two poles of heights 8 m and 13 m stand on level ground. If the distance between their feet is 12 m, find the distance between their tops.
questions.answer: The tops are joined by a slant line. The horizontal separation is 12 m and the vertical difference is 13 - 8 = 5 m. These are the legs of a right triangle whose hypotenuse is the distance between the tops: d = sqrt(12^2 + 5^2) = sqrt(144 + 25) = sqrt(169) = 13 m.

questions.question: Give one difference between similar figures and congruent figures.
questions.answer: Similar figures have the same shape but may differ in size (corresponding sides are proportional). Congruent figures have the same shape AND the same size (corresponding sides are equal). Thus congruence is the special case of similarity where the scale factor equals 1.
questions.explanation: Size differs for similar, equal for congruent.

questions.question: In triangle ABC, DE || BC. If AD = 1.5 cm, DB = 3 cm and AE = 1 cm, find EC.
questions.answer: By BPT, AD/DB = AE/EC. So 1.5/3 = 1/EC, i.e. 0.5 = 1/EC, giving EC = 2 cm.

questions.question: The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is 4:9. If the base of the smaller triangle is 6 cm, find the base of the larger triangle.
questions.answer: Ratio of areas 4:9, so the ratio of corresponding sides is sqrt(4):sqrt(9) = 2:3. If the smaller base is 6 cm, then smaller:larger = 2:3, so 6/larger = 2/3, giving larger base = (6 x 3)/2 = 9 cm.
questions.explanation: Side ratio is square root of area ratio.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

In triangle PQR a line ST is drawn so that angle PST = angle PQR, with S on PQ and T on PR. Given PS = 3 cm, SQ = 5 cm, PT = 3.6 cm.

(i) Which two angles are common or equal in triangles PST and PQR?
(ii) By which criterion is triangle PST ~ triangle PQR?
(iii) Write the proportionality of sides.
(iv) Find PR.
questions.answer:
(i) angle P is common to both triangles, and angle PST = angle PQR (given).
(ii) By the AA similarity criterion, triangle PST ~ triangle PQR.
(iii) PS/PQ = PT/PR = ST/QR.
(iv) PQ = PS + SQ = 3 + 5 = 8 cm. Using PS/PQ = PT/PR: 3/8 = 3.6/PR, so PR = (3.6 x 8)/3 = 28.8/3 = 9.6 cm.
questions.explanation: AA similarity then a proportion for PR.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

Two triangles ABC and DEF have sides AB = 6 cm, BC = 8 cm, CA = 10 cm and DE = 9 cm, EF = 12 cm, FD = 15 cm.

(i) Compute the three ratios of corresponding sides.
(ii) Are the triangles similar? Name the criterion.
(iii) State the scale factor.
(iv) If the perimeter of triangle ABC is 24 cm, find the perimeter of triangle DEF.
questions.answer:
(i) AB/DE = 6/9 = 2/3, BC/EF = 8/12 = 2/3, CA/FD = 10/15 = 2/3.
(ii) All three ratios are equal, so by the SSS similarity criterion triangle ABC ~ triangle DEF.
(iii) Scale factor (ABC to DEF) = 2/3.
(iv) Perimeters are in the same ratio as sides: perimeter(ABC)/perimeter(DEF) = 2/3, so 24/perimeter(DEF) = 2/3, giving perimeter(DEF) = 36 cm.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

In triangle ABC, a line DE is drawn parallel to BC, cutting AB at D and AC at E.

(i) State the Basic Proportionality Theorem for this figure.
(ii) Which pair of triangles are equal in area in the standard proof, and why?
(iii) Show that triangle ADE ~ triangle ABC.
(iv) Write the resulting equal ratios.
questions.answer:
(i) DE || BC implies AD/DB = AE/EC.
(ii) Triangles BDE and CDE are equal in area because they have the same base DE and lie between the same parallels DE and BC.
(iii) In triangles ADE and ABC, angle A is common and angle ADE = angle ABC (corresponding angles, DE || BC). By AA, triangle ADE ~ triangle ABC.
(iv) AD/AB = AE/AC = DE/BC.
questions.explanation: BPT statement, the equal-area step, and the AA similarity that follows.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

In triangle ABC, D and E are points on AB and AC. Four measurements are taken: AD = 2 cm, DB = 4 cm, AE = 3 cm, EC = 6 cm.

(i) Find AD/DB.
(ii) Find AE/EC.
(iii) Is DE parallel to BC? Which theorem justifies your answer?
(iv) If DE is parallel to BC and BC = 9 cm, find DE.
questions.answer:
(i) AD/DB = 2/4 = 1/2.
(ii) AE/EC = 3/6 = 1/2.
(iii) Since AD/DB = AE/EC = 1/2, by the converse of the Basic Proportionality Theorem DE is parallel to BC.
(iv) With DE || BC, triangle ADE ~ triangle ABC, so DE/BC = AD/AB = 2/(2+4) = 1/3. Hence DE = (1/3) x 9 = 3 cm.
questions.explanation: Converse of BPT, then the similar-triangle ratio for DE.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

Triangle ABC ~ triangle DEF. Corresponding sides AB = 5 cm and DE = 10 cm are given. The area of triangle ABC is 30 cm^2.

(i) Find the ratio of corresponding sides.
(ii) Find the ratio of their areas.
(iii) Find the area of triangle DEF.
(iv) If the perimeter of triangle ABC is 20 cm, find the perimeter of triangle DEF.
questions.answer:
(i) AB:DE = 5:10 = 1:2.
(ii) Ratio of areas = (1:2)^2 = 1:4.
(iii) area(ABC)/area(DEF) = 1/4, so 30/area(DEF) = 1/4, giving area(DEF) = 120 cm^2.
(iv) Perimeters are in the side ratio 1:2, so perimeter(DEF) = 2 x 20 = 40 cm.
questions.explanation: Side ratio 1:2 gives area ratio 1:4; perimeter scales linearly.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

A triangle ABC is right-angled at B. An altitude BD is drawn to the hypotenuse AC. It is found that AD = 3.6 cm and AC = 10 cm.

(i) Name the two triangles similar to triangle ABC.
(ii) Using triangle ADB ~ triangle ABC, find AB.
(iii) Find DC.
(iv) Verify BC using BC^2 = AC x DC.
questions.answer:
(i) Triangle ADB ~ triangle ABC and triangle BDC ~ triangle ABC.
(ii) From triangle ADB ~ triangle ABC, AB^2 = AC x AD = 10 x 3.6 = 36, so AB = 6 cm.
(iii) DC = AC - AD = 10 - 3.6 = 6.4 cm.
(iv) BC^2 = AC x DC = 10 x 6.4 = 64, so BC = 8 cm. Check: AB^2 + BC^2 = 36 + 64 = 100 = 10^2 = AC^2, confirming Pythagoras theorem.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

At a certain time of day, a girl of height 1.2 m casts a shadow of length 0.9 m. Nearby, a lamp post casts a shadow of length 3.6 m at the same moment.

(i) Why do the girl and the lamp post form similar triangles?
(ii) Write the proportion relating heights and shadows.
(iii) Find the height of the lamp post.
(iv) State one everyday use of this method.
questions.answer:
(i) Because the sun's rays fall at the same angle at the same time, both triangles have a right angle at the ground and the same angle of elevation of the sun, so by AA they are similar.
(ii) (height of girl)/(shadow of girl) = (height of lamp post)/(shadow of lamp post).
(iii) 1.2/0.9 = H/3.6, so H = (1.2 x 3.6)/0.9 = 4.32/0.9 = 4.8 m.
(iv) This method is used to find the heights of trees, buildings and towers that cannot be measured directly (using shadows).
questions.explanation: Similar triangles from shadows; solve for height.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

A rectangular park ABCD has length AB = 40 m and breadth BC = 30 m. A straight path runs along the diagonal AC.

(i) What kind of angle is angle ABC?
(ii) Which theorem gives the length of the diagonal?
(iii) Find the length of the diagonal AC.
(iv) If a person walks along AB and BC instead of the diagonal, how much extra distance is covered?
questions.answer:
(i) angle ABC is a right angle (90 degrees), since ABCD is a rectangle.
(ii) The Pythagoras theorem gives the diagonal.
(iii) AC = sqrt(AB^2 + BC^2) = sqrt(40^2 + 30^2) = sqrt(1600 + 900) = sqrt(2500) = 50 m.
(iv) Walking AB + BC = 40 + 30 = 70 m; the diagonal is 50 m; extra distance = 70 - 50 = 20 m.
questions.explanation: Diagonal by Pythagoras; compare path lengths.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

A student claims that any two right-angled triangles are always similar.

(i) Is the claim correct? Justify.
(ii) What extra condition would make two right triangles similar?
(iii) Give an example of two right triangles that are NOT similar.
(iv) Name the criterion that would confirm similarity when it holds.
questions.answer:
(i) The claim is not correct. Having a right angle each gives only ONE pair of equal angles, which is not enough for similarity.
(ii) They are similar if a second pair of angles is also equal (AA), or if the two legs are in the same ratio (SAS with the right angle included).
(iii) A 3-4-5 right triangle and a 5-12-13 right triangle are both right-angled but their acute angles differ, so they are not similar.
(iv) The AA criterion (or SAS using the right angle and the two legs) confirms similarity when the extra condition holds.
questions.explanation: One equal angle is not enough; AA or SAS needed.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

Two similar triangles have areas 100 cm^2 and 64 cm^2.

(i) Find the ratio of their areas in simplest form.
(ii) Find the ratio of their corresponding sides.
(iii) If the smallest side of the larger triangle is 15 cm, find the smallest side of the smaller triangle.
(iv) Find the ratio of their perimeters.
questions.answer:
(i) Ratio of areas = 100:64 = 25:16.
(ii) Ratio of corresponding sides = sqrt(25):sqrt(16) = 5:4.
(iii) Larger:smaller = 5:4, so 15/(smaller side) = 5/4, giving smaller side = (15 x 4)/5 = 12 cm.
(iv) Perimeters are in the side ratio 5:4.
questions.explanation: Side ratio is the square root of the area ratio.
